one_line: Consent-bound proof exchange that keeps private records out of agent conversations.
what_it_does: A two-site wallet/verifier workflow where a verifier requests derived claims, a wallet firewall negotiates a minimal request, a person approves one-time export, and the agent carries the proof without final-submission authority.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP is central to the shared, consent-bound two-site workflow: structured tools enforce minimal disclosure, one-time export, and human gating in a way generic UI driving cannot comparably guarantee.
leverage_evidence: About text describes verifier-published claims, wallet request firewall, counterproposal, one-time wallet_export_proof, and no final-submit tool.
Frame sheet shows credential wallet and fellowship verifier connected, then negotiation panels.
execution_rationale: The packet presents a coherent privacy workflow with explicit safety states and visible wallet/verifier surfaces; exact end-to-end operation is claimed rather than fully observed.
execution_evidence: Three production artifacts are claimed: verifier, wallet, and shared flow.
Frames show consistent hero and dark negotiation interfaces.
Description includes rejection, counterproposal, approval, expiry, and handoff states.
impact_rationale: It addresses a concrete, consequential problem—proving eligibility without exposing identity-rich records—for applicants and organizations.
impact_evidence: Examples include age, enrollment, GPA threshold, and residency claims.
The design explicitly keeps birth date, GPA, transcript, address, student ID, and name private.
creativity_rationale: The minimal-proof courier and request-negotiation interaction is a fresh, memorable application of WebMCP and privacy-by-design.
creativity_evidence: Agent carries derived proof rather than private records.
Unsafe requests yield a machine-readable counterproposal instead of silent over-sharing.
usability_note: Visible review, recipient/purpose/expiry disclosure, and human-only approval support trust; some small-text states are hard to inspect in the contact sheet.
standouts: WebMCP is a structural security boundary, not a button wrapper.
advance_reason: High-leverage, high-impact privacy workflow with substantial evidence and a distinctive interaction model.

one_line: Bring user-owned MCP capabilities into any page as controlled WebMCP tools.
what_it_does: Discovers MCP servers, classifies risk, obtains user grants, dynamically registers tools, bridges calls, audits activity, and revokes leases.
leverage_rationale: The product's entire purpose is moving user-owned capabilities into a browser-native agent surface; dynamic registration, consent, audit, and revocation are not comparably reproducible through ordinary UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Description explicitly says WebMCP is the only surface enabling this without an extension or bespoke runtime.
Workflow covers discover, classify, approve, register, execute, audit, and revoke.
execution_rationale: The concept and lifecycle are unusually coherent, with risk classification and revocation accounted for; no video lowers certainty about end-to-end execution.
execution_evidence: About text specifies MCP bridge to tools/call and visible request/completion/failure audit.
Frame sheets show repeated capability/agent dashboard states with red/green status panels and metrics.
impact_rationale: It could materially reduce duplicated integrations for users and sites while preserving user control over powerful capabilities.
impact_evidence: Targets existing MCP users and websites such as Gmail, GitHub, Notion, Slack, and Drive.
User grants and one-click revocation address real trust and integration friction.
creativity_rationale: The reverse-WebMCP framing and capability portability model are original and ambitiously pursued as a full lifecycle.
creativity_evidence: Explicit inversion of the usual page-to-agent model.
Combines dynamic tool registration with risk annotations, leases, audit, and revoke.
usability_note: Consent and audit affordances are strong; the contact sheets show dense dashboard states but small labels.
red_flags: No submitted video; evidence relies on frames and written description.
standouts: WebMCP-in-reverse is a compelling product thesis.
Revocation makes the capability lifecycle legible and bounded.
advance_reason: Exceptional WebMCP leverage and a novel, coherent agent-infrastructure product.

one_line: A portable learning protocol that lets sites issue signed proof of what readers learned.
what_it_does: A user-owned vault stores signed learning receipts; tagged pages expose tools to inspect prerequisites, adapt instruction, and issue receipts that derive a learner model and next steps.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP connects arbitrary teaching pages, the learner's local vault, and an agent through structured tools; generic automation cannot as reliably preserve portable signed state across sites.
leverage_evidence: Two tags expose six tools for teaching, prerequisite checks, adaptation, and receipt signing.
Vault is browser/disk-owned with no account and is designed to work across pages.
execution_rationale: The protocol and learner-model concept are well specified and supported by gallery/packaging, but there is no video and end-to-end learning completion is not shown.
execution_evidence: Description details signed receipts, ability bands, memory schedule, and adaptive prerequisites.
Three gallery images are listed, but no video frame evidence is supplied.
impact_rationale: Learners benefit from continuity and adaptive review across the fragmented web, a clear problem for self-directed education.
impact_evidence: Targets people learning from blogs, courses, and reference pages.
Portable state avoids each site starting from zero.
creativity_rationale: A web-wide learning protocol with signed receipts and a six-dimensional ability model is a notably original and ambitious interaction model.
creativity_evidence: Sites issue signed proof of learning into a user-owned vault.
Advanced learning credits prerequisites and schedules future review.
usability_note: No-account local vault is promising, though the packet does not show the learner flow in motion.
red_flags: No submitted video; end-to-end behavior is claimed rather than demonstrated.
standouts: Portable, signed learning state is a strong protocol-level idea.
advance_reason: Distinctive, high-impact education protocol with strong WebMCP leverage despite limited runtime evidence.

one_line: A pinboard that fences stranger-written text before agents consume it.
what_it_does: Marks every user-written field as untrusted in tool output, visibly quarantines it for humans, logs only IDs/counts, and makes overrides and deletion human-only.
leverage_rationale: WebMCP metadata and structured untrusted-content boundaries change agent reliability and safety at the exact point where prompt injection enters tool results; this is more than UI automation.
leverage_evidence: Description says every pinner-written field carries untrustedContentHint:true and a forgery-proof fence.
Claims a live seeded prompt injection, forged fence-closer, false positive, and human override behavior.
execution_rationale: The packet describes layered model/client/human defenses and even identifies and fixes a CSS hidden-state bug; frames show pinboard, quarantine chips, and tool console.
execution_evidence: Three frame sheets cover pinboard, tool console, and WebMCP surface.
About text documents 14 seeded pins and safety cases.
Description reports a CSS cascade bug was found and corrected.
impact_rationale: Prompt injection from user-generated content is a real problem for any agent-curated board or knowledge workspace, and the mitigation is directly useful.
impact_evidence: Targets stranger-written captions, notes, board names, and descriptions.
Activity log avoids quoting attacker-controlled text.
creativity_rationale: Treating provenance and untrusted-content handling as the product interaction, with synchronized machine and human fences, is a focused and original safety concept.
creativity_evidence: Three-layer signaling to client, model, and human.
Human-only quarantine overrides and no-delete tool are deliberate constraints.
usability_note: Visible quarantine chips and one-line warnings make trust state legible; false-positive clearing is explicitly supported.
red_flags: Claims a fixed CSS issue in the narrative; current runtime correction is not independently observed.
standouts: Excellent alignment between security model, tool metadata, and human-visible UI.
advance_reason: Strong, focused WebMCP safety innovation with concrete attack evidence and coherent execution.

one_line: Git-like PCB design review and handoff where agents propose and people approve.
what_it_does: A local-first circuit-board workspace lets agents create/inspect/propose revisions, while humans approve changes, preserve history, fork checkpoints, review incoming work, and refuse unsupported fabrication decisions.
leverage_rationale: Structured board inspection, proposal previews, approval, revision history, fork/handoff, and conflict handling make agent collaboration materially safer and more precise than UI driving.
leverage_evidence: Transcript describes create, inspect, propose, preview, visible approval, revision, checkpoint, fork, adoption, and conflict behavior.
Agents cannot silently merge or fabricate; incoming approvals remain unreviewed.
execution_rationale: The product demonstrates a coherent review lifecycle and honestly limits claims around hardware readiness; submitted video frames and transcript support the central flow.
execution_evidence: Video is 167 seconds with transcript describing board creation through handoff.
Three frame sheets show the product states.
Transcript explicitly distinguishes modeled zero-error compilation from a manufacturing certificate.
impact_rationale: PCB designers and hardware teams face expensive board spins and need trustworthy review/handoff; the product addresses that risk directly.
impact_evidence: About text identifies missing requirements, unverified parts, pad layouts, and physical fit as costly failure modes.
Human approval and preserved history support engineering accountability.
creativity_rationale: Applying Git-like revision and human-gated agent collaboration to PCB design is a memorable, original interaction model with ambitious handoff semantics.
creativity_evidence: Protected checkpoints, local forks, incoming unreviewed approvals, and explicit conflict refusal.
Plain-English explanations sit beside exact parts and evidence.
usability_note: Read-only review, previews, revision history, and explicit limits support safe collaboration; hardware claims are appropriately bounded.
red_flags: Product is a modeled design/review system, not proof of a complete manufacturable circuit or iPhone connection.
standouts: Honest refusal to equate clean CAD checks with fabrication safety.
Excellent revision and handoff model for agent-assisted engineering.
advance_reason: Distinctive, well-evidenced agent-native PCB review workflow with real engineering value.
